svg.text: Call flow: what happens, in order
The order of steps is fixed. An early exit at any step is also audited and counted in metrics.
Steps 1-5 do not touch the API yet: invalid, unsafe and
After a write timeout the gateway does NOT retry blindly: it checks with a
GET from the rule's template whether the action already happened.
The gateway is stateless: many copies can run, coordinating only through DynamoDB.
Status: design. The gateway itself is not built yet (Stage 2).
Status: design. Built so far: mock providers (local + Lambda), scripted agent, runner.

Experiment: how the numbers are made
Same tasks, same faults, different protection. Duplicates are counted from provider state, not from what the agent says.
Solid = built and working. Dashed grey = planned, not built yet.
config A: the agent calls the providers directly, no gateway
runner counts duplicates by reading the provider state (not the agent's report)
What fault injection does to one request
Same request, same fault, in every config.
A retry has a new attempt number,
so it can get a different outcome.
Run A baseline, 200 tasks per profile (3 attempts per step):
low: 100% success, 3.5% of tasks have a duplicate
high: 96.5% success, 17% of tasks have a duplicate
Goal for B and C: duplicates down to 0 without lowering success.
Metrics: success rate, tasks with duplicates, p95 latency, calls per task.
